title: Talent integration 14-day accelerator: hiring plan & interview rubric (draft)
summary: Working draft: focused hiring plan and condensed interview rubric for fast-turnover roles (support, onboarding specialists, junior SRE). Includes a 14-day activation checklist to reduce time-to-productivity and an interview scorecard tuned for hire-for-attitude/hypergrowth contexts.
content:
Context and objective:

This is an iterative People Ops artifact for roles where we historically see higher churn or where time-to-impact is critical (onboarding specialists, Tier-1 support, junior SRE/oncall triage). Goal: compress a reliable integration path into the first 14 calendar days while improving hiring signal quality so managers can make faster offers with confidence.

Audience:
- Hiring managers for high-volume hiring roles
- Recruiters and sourcers
- Interviewers (ICs + managers)
- Onboarding / L&D partners

High-level approach (thesis):
1) Hire for three non-negotiable signals: grit (learning velocity), customer empathy, and systems curiosity.
2) Use a short, evidence-focused interview loop (2–3 touchpoints) that yields artifacts (work sample, roleplay notes) rather than long subjective feedback.
3) Pre-boarding + day-0 checklist reduces first-week admin overhead so hires spend >60% of week 1 on role-specific systems and shadowing.
4) Measure activation via a 14-day ramp scorecard (training completion, shadow hours, first independent ticket/handoff).

Hiring plan snapshot (for a single hire funnel, scaleable to cohort hiring):
- Stage 0: Sourcing brief (2 days)
  - Role profile: 60–80% operational work, 20–40% cross-team communication
  - Minimum screening checklist for recruiter: resume evidence of structured troubleshooting, one example of direct customer communication, and >6 months in a role with measurable outputs
  - Slack outreach script template included (see linked artifacts)

- Stage 1: Recruiter phone screen (20–30m) — goal: confirm signal and culture fit
  - Quick situational prompts (2x) and one competency story probe (STAR)
  - Pass if candidate demonstrates clear examples of prior ownership and learning from mistakes

- Stage 2: Work sample + manager interview (60–75m combined)
  - Work sample: time boxed (30–45m asynchronous) — triage a synthetic ticket or debug a short runbook; candidate submits notes + next steps. Use rubric to score for clarity, troubleshooting steps, and escalation judgment.
  - Manager interview (30m): focus on role expectations, career trajectory, and cultural fit.

- Stage 3: Final rubric panel (30m) — cross-functional interviewer (customer success or product) to validate empathy and communication.

Timeline target: offer extended within 5 business days of initial screen.

Interview rubric (condensed, evidence-first):
Fields collected by interviewer (use the short scorecard):
- Signal1_learning-velocity (0,1,2) — examples: rapid upskilling story, side-project with concrete results, clear debrief on a past failure + applied learnings.
- Signal2_customer-empathy (0,1,2) — examples: roleplay with upset customer shows calm, active listening, and a solution orientation.
- Signal3_systems-curiosity (0,1,2) — examples: asks clarifying diagnostic questions, proposes next-step hypotheses, references monitoring/logging heuristics.
- Work-sample-quality (0,1,2) — clarity, structure, steps to reproduce, escalation path.
- Communication-written (0,1,2) — concision, appropriate tone, completeness.
- Cultural-add (0,1,2) — alignment to Redwood values: shipping, reliability mindset, openness.
- Hire-recommendation: Yes / No / Hire-with-coaching
- Notes-to-hiring-manager: free text (required)

Scoring guidance: 0 = insufficient/unsafe; 1 = competent with coaching needed; 2 = independent and high-confidence. A typical pass threshold: total >=9/12 with no 0s in customer-empathy or communication-written for customer-facing roles. Document exceptions in notes.

Work sample templates (examples to reuse):
- Support triage ticket: candidate reads a transcript and logs the steps to reproduce, gravity assessment, proposed first response, and escalation plan.
- Oncall playbook check: given a short incident description and monitoring snapshot, write a short runbook and rollback checklist.

Pre-boarding & day-0 checklist (aim: reduce first-day admin to <2 hours)
- Pre-boarding (HR/recruiter): send onboarding guide, first-week schedule, account setup checklist, Zoom links to buddy and manager, and an optional 30-minute pre-onboard touchpoint (role expectations).
- IT: create accounts two business days before start; ensure laptop imaging + necessary credentials are ready.
- Compliance: send any required paperwork with clear due dates.

Day 0 (first calendar day) prioritized schedule (sample):
- 09:00 — manager welcome (30m): expectations, 14-day ramp goals, quick team intro
- 09:45 — IT + security check (30m)
- 10:30 — buddy intro + shadow schedule (15m)
- 11:00 — lunch (team) optional
- 13:00 — systems orientation (1h): core dashboards, ticketsystems, runbooks
- 15:00 — small first task assigned (workable within 90m), manager sets clear acceptance criteria

First 14-day activation scorecard (manager fills on day 14) — target KPIs and yes/no gates:
- Mandatory items (gates):
  - Completed 3 core trainings (ticketing, incident logging, communication templates): Y/N
  - Buddy-shadow hours >= 8: Y/N
  - Submitted first independent ticket or runbook change with manager review: Y/N
- Performance metrics (scored 0–2):
  - Operational accuracy (tickets resolved without rework)
  - Communication clarity (internal & customer-facing)
  - Time-to-first-independent-action (days)
- Recommendation at day 14: Continue normal ramp / Continued coaching (14d) / Re-evaluate (30d)

Manager playbook highlights (practical tips):
- Use micro-goals each day (3 tasks max) and document them in the new hire’s onboarding doc.
- Do not assign >1 critical path ticket in week 1 without paired support.
- Run a short 15-minute check-in at EOD for the first 7 days. Capture blockers in JIRA ticket "HR-ONBOARD-ISSUES" for tracking.

Onboarding content inventory (to create or update):
- 1) Minimal role runbooks (2–3 pages) — should be consumable in 30–45m
- 2) Roleplay scripts for customer empathy scenarios
- 3) Short video walkthroughs (5–8m) for core tools (ticketing, dashboarding)
- 4) First-week practice tasks with acceptance criteria

Open questions / risks (callouts for people ops):
- How to scale buddy program for cohort hires without burning out senior ICs? Proposal: assign a rotation of micro-buddies (2 per week) instead of a single long-term buddy.
- What’s an acceptable market time-to-offer? Current target 5 business days is aggressive for high-volume roles — need recruiter bandwidth analysis (see JIRA HR-4567).
- Attrition signal: collect a short exit pulse for hires who leave before 90 days; target n>=12 before we make structural changes.

Notes to self (draft tone):
- Need to sync with L&D to convert runbook checklist into 3 short Loom videos.
- Pull last 6 months of first-30-day success metrics for onboarding specialists from HRBI — ask analytics team for CSV.
- Validate rubric thresholds with two hiring managers next week (Miguel and Priya volunteered).

Appendix: sample recruiter outreach (short):
Hi <name>,
We’re hiring a fast-paced role at Redwood Inference focused on customer-facing operations and troubleshooting. The team moves quickly and values curiosity and clear communication over formal credentials. If you’re open, can we do a 20m screen this week?

—End of draft—

(Formatting intentionally simple — this is a working doc. Please add comments inline and flag any items that should be escalated to "people-ops/policy".)
